Treatment summary
Patient prseented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of low back pain and stiffness. The reported
mechanism is consistent with the symptoms described, and the presentation is a plausible account of a soft-tissue strain. Over the
course of 27 visits, care consisted of manual therapy, targeted home exercise instruction, and graduated strengthening, which is a
typical and expected course for this type of injury. Frequency of visits decreased steadily as range of motion and pain scores
improved, and the patient was discharged to self-directed exercise once goals were met. Imaging and physical examination
findings clearly confirm a lumbar srtain consistent with the collision. Review of the available history shows no prior injury to the
lumbar region. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service rendered with no duplicated procedures.
Prognosis is good with full recovery anticipated.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
